newsitem.title: UK: Fall in UK car crime cuts insurance costs -report.
newsitem.headline: Fall in UK car crime cuts insurance costs -report.

text.p: The cost of thefts from car fleets in the UK fell in the first quarter, according to a report from fleet management company VELO Group.

"The continued fall in car crime...has had a marked effect on the cost of theft per fleet vehicle, with a fall of nearly 24 percent this quarter alone," VELO said in its sixth quarterly Fleet Insurance Statistics Report.
The overall incidence of car crime, including vehicle theft, was down 2.8 percent in the first quarter, compared with 17 percent in the whole of 1996.
The report, based on some 30,000 claims, also shows that many insurance claims are concentrated on a small number of drivers.

"One sixth of drivers were responsible for half of all claims and around half of the total costs," VELO said, adding that the worst 13 drivers ran up 102 claims totalling 350,000 stg in the last year.

VELO's survey of vehicle repair costs by manufacturer shows the gap narrowing between the cheapest and most expensive. Fiat remained in first place, while Peugeot PEUP PA moved to second from third, followed by Land/Range Rover BMWG.F and Ford F.N.
The report includes average repair costs for many cars by model and by vehicle class.
VELO Motor Accident Management Limited, a part of Aon Risk Services Limited AOC.N and VELO Limited, provides accident management for over 110,000 vehicles.
VELO Limited, a part of Dresdner Kleinwort Benson DRSD.F, provides fleet management and financing services to more than 18,000 vehicles.
